question: Which of the following is the correct unit mass of sodium?
solution:
The correct answer is __**23 u**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The atomic mass of sodium (Na) is **23 unified atomic mass units (u)**.
 
• Sodium is represented by the symbol **Na** on the periodic table.
 
• Sodium's atomic number is **11**, indicating it has 11 protons.
 
• The atomic mass is calculated primarily from the number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Unified Atomic Mass Unit (u)**

 
 
• It is a standard unit of mass that quantifies mass on an atomic or molecular scale.
 
• 1 unified atomic mass unit is defined as one twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.
 
 
 
• **Periodic Table**
 
 
• It is a tabular display of the chemical elements, organized on the basis of their atomic numbers, electron configurations, and recurring chemical properties.
 
• Elements are presented in order of increasing atomic number.
 
 
 
• **Isotopes**
 
 
• Isotopes are variants of a particular chemical element that have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
 
• Sodium has several isotopes, but only sodium-23 is stable and naturally abundant.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Properties of Sodium**
 
 
• Sodium is a highly reactive metal and is part of the alkali metal group.
 
• It reacts vigorously with water to form sodium hydroxide and hydrogen gas.
